author: toriumnetwork
text:
Dear Torium Miners,

Our iOS development process is moving forward at full speed.

Getting the required approvals from Apple took longer than we expected. Since this involved legal and bureaucratic procedures, we see this as a normal part of the process. However, we were not able to hit our original goal of launching the iOS app in June.

The good news: Apple has finally approved our membership, and the iOS version of the Torium Network app will be live in July.

Thank you for waiting patiently and believing in us throughout this process.

During this time, Dr. Kah Seng Lim from Veridian Systems officially joined Torium. We mentioned this in our partnership announcement, and we are now working together to prepare our infrastructure for the program Veridian Systems plans to launch in Q2 2027.

We understand how important real product verification is in the pharmaceutical industry. Fighting counterfeit and copied products is not just important, it is a milestone mission.

Alongside all of this, we continue to improve, test, and strengthen our infrastructure.

We have also added games inside the Torium app. The more time you spend in the Torium app, the more valuable it becomes for the activity of the network. In our infrastructure, more active nodes means a stronger network.

We have welcomed the first members of our Ambassador Program into the team. We are working day and night to improve our operations, and thanks to this program, Torium is already reaching wider communities.

A huge thank you to our ambassadors.

Now is not the time to rest.

The wind is behind us. Awareness is growing. We have launched our first partnership. Our infrastructure is in a strong place, and it will only get stronger.

And on top of all that, Torium is still only a 4-month-old project.

We could not have reached this point without your support. We are deeply grateful, and we are working harder than ever.

July will be a fast month full of updates.

Thank you, Torium Family.

author: ghostex_dev
text:
Hey all! 

Please upgrade to 5.0 by clicking on the button on the top left of the app's window if you're a regular user, I'm really proud of this update :)

And if you've tried Ghostex before but had any issues with performance or bugs then I hope you try this new version because it's honestly much better! 

I just released 5.0 today and it's the biggest jump in performance and features  in all the past releases.

You should notice that all of these are much faster now: 

1. Switching between warm terminals and warm views (source/browser/kanban/docs) is instant now and the delay is fully gone. 

2. The sidebar scroll area is much lighter and smoother to scroll and reacts instantly compared to before.

3. The Kanban board actions were optimized heavily (local first design which syncs with the beads db).

(Warm means they aren't sleeping to conserve resources) 

There's also a new project view called docs that combines: 
1. The Claude app's ″Artifacts″ feature
2. With Excalidraw
3. Plus Plannonator's md files annotation features :)

Just tell your agent to create or edit one of these in the docs folder: 
- A new html prototype/explainer
- An excalidraw drawing
- An md plan or PRD doc

You'll be able to collaborate with the agent very well because of this feature and being able to annotate & ask for edits or even by just editing things yourself and asking the agent to read the edits :) 

Other important things:
- Fully ported the backend logic for gxserver bg service to Rust for better performance than the old TypeScript code. 

- Released an easier to navigate settings modal

- Fixed a ton of bugs

- Made Android & iOS apps auto scale the terminal on connect

- Merged the ability to set any dock/switcher icon you want for the app while it's running (first PR by the app's biggest supporter @Nite_I_Am!)   

- Added instructions on how to use computer use and browser use.

- Made a ton of progress on the port from macOS swift/appkit to Rust/GPUI (Zed IDE's fast framework) which would let this app run on windows and linux (need contributors to help, this is a huge undertaking :)
+ Much more

I was on the subway in NYC, talking to my Hermes agent thru Telegram.

Loved Hermes. Telegram, not so much. How sick would it be to interface with my agent through something as sleek as the ChatGPT app.

I'd never built an iOS app, and I don't really know Swift. The last app I tried to make was a calculator, when I was 15. But I wanted this one enough that I used AI to figure the whole thing out - building an AI client with AI. Big brain move.

That app is Hermex.

It feels like the ChatGPT app, except it's pointed at my own Hermes agent. And now I reach for Hermex over the ChatGPT app for most things.

Still early, but if that sounds like your kind of thing, check it out 👇

author: ewtnews
text:
For many Catholics, faith formation often competes with busy schedules and endless digital distractions. Fio, a Catholic audio streaming platform, hopes to change that by putting faith-filled content at listeners’ fingertips.

Dubbed “the Catholic alternative to Spotify,” the platform offers a growing library of podcasts, audiobooks, and music, giving users a way to stay connected to their faith wherever life takes them.

Currently, Fio is being used in over 100 countries, is host to over 100,000 hours of Catholic content, and has over 1,000 Catholic creators putting their work onto the platform.

Will Hickl, co-founder of Fio, has been in the music industry for 15 years as a musician and founder of the Catholic record label NOVUM RECORDS. During his career, he realized that secular platforms were not built for faith-based work — it was difficult to stand out, there was no fair compensation, and there was no community around it.

With this in mind, Hickl, and co-founder Peter Buonincontro, launched Fio in 2023. The first version of the app hosted podcasts alone. The following year music was added, and the following year — thanks to a generous investor — the platform was able to host audiobooks and grow their collection of content. 

In an interview with EWTN News, Hickl shared that the platform’s “North Star” is the fact that he cares deeply about the artists and content creators.

“We are a platform who, because we care, weʼre paying a penny per stream, which is already three to four times what Spotify pays,” he explained. “We want to offer better exposure and tooling. In fact, we already offer better exposure because a musician doesnʼt have to compete with 10 million other musicians. Thereʼs only maybe like 100, maybe 200 artists on the platform right now…thereʼs greater discoverability.”

For creators, he hopes they would know that Fio “is the one that genuinely cares about them more than Apple or Spotify ever will.”

Currently, Fio offers three subscription levels for listeners — free, premium, and audiobooks +. While users who subscribe to the platform for free will have to listen to advertisements, Hickl pointed out that these ads “are reserved and curated for Catholic businesses, Catholic ministries, and then Catholic artists on the platform.”

He also emphasized that these faith-based advertisements can also serve as a “cultural safeguard” so that parents who may be listening with children present don’t have to worry about inappropriate advertisements being played, as is the case with many secular platforms.

Hickl explained that Fio aims to serve three different cohorts: Catholic creators, consumers, and businesses.

“We are an artist first platform. We want to give you the best exposure, the best economics than any other platform,” he said. “For consumers, we want to give you greater choice, a better experience in terms of what you find, what your kids are exposed to. The third would be Catholic businesses who canʼt target based on religion on Facebook or Google or YouTube or anything like that. So weʼre offering a greater targeting mechanism, greater value in that regard.”

For those seeking to have their content on Fio, they must go through a submission and review process. Before their content is accepted, creators must affirm that they are practicing Catholics who accept the teachings of the Church. They must also verify that their work was not primarily created by artificial intelligence. Lastly, each creator goes through a manual review process by the Fio team before their work is allowed to be on the platform.

Looking to the future, the team at Fio is working on creating original content for the platform as well as being able to host video podcasts and music videos. Additionally, they are working to give Fio a more “liturgical feel.” For example, if there’s an important saint’s feast day, Fio would make suggestions to listeners of a podcast that talks about the saint or a song inspired by the saint.

Hickl hopes that one day more artists will “be more excited about sharing their Fio link than the Spotify link.”

He added that he hopes Catholics “would know I can trust this platform, it can and should be a part of my every day, because thereʼs so much treasure to discover.”

“Thatʼs something I say a lot, which is that the Church has an immense amount of treasure and we just donʼt know about it. And so I want people to know the treasure is here and Fio is a place where itʼs aggregated,” he said.

Fio can be downloaded on iOS, Android, and streamed through your web browser.

text:
OpenClaw is now available on both iOS and Android.

What’s interesting is that your phone isn’t the AI assistant itself, it’s simply the interface.

The real AI agent runs on a Gateway that you host and control, not on a company’s servers or a third-party cloud.

You choose exactly what it can access.

Camera, location, contacts, calendar every permission is optional and granted only if you allow it.

You also bring your own model and API key, whether that’s Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or another provider.

But the biggest story isn’t the app itself.

Until recently, Apple was reluctant to allow highly agentic AI apps on the App Store because of the level of device access and user trust they require.

OpenClaw’s approval signals that this is beginning to change.

For the first time, a self-hosted, open-source AI agent can sit alongside apps like ChatGPT and Gemini on the App Store.

That’s a much bigger milestone than it might seem at first glance.

author: nguynhu45025293
text:
China Wins: Why Open-Source AI Becomes the Default — and Why $TAO Matters

There are rare moments in technology when a policy decision reveals which business models are fragile and which ones are inevitable.

I think we just witnessed one of those moments in AI.

Over the past few weeks, the U.S. government has started intervening directly in how frontier AI models are released. Anthropic was reportedly forced to restrict access to its newest models. OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 rollout also appears to be staged through a limited preview for trusted partners before broader release. The official justification is national security: cybersecurity, biosecurity, export controls, and preventing frontier capabilities from reaching adversaries.

I am not dismissing those concerns.

The risks are real.

But markets do not only price intentions. Markets price behavior.

And what enterprises, developers, founders, and investors are seeing is this: if you build your critical infrastructure on closed frontier models, a government letter can change your entire roadmap overnight.

That is the moment open-source AI stops being “cheaper but worse” and becomes “good enough, controllable, and impossible to take away.”

This is why the “China wins” thesis is no longer just a meme.

It is becoming a serious possibility.

America Is Winning the Benchmark Race. China Is Winning Distribution.

For the past three years, the U.S. has dominated the AI narrative through frontier models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, Meta, and the cloud hyperscalers.

The best models. The most compute. The deepest capital markets. The strongest research talent. The most powerful cloud infrastructure.

If you define the AI race as “who has the smartest model at the frontier,” America is still in an extremely strong position.

But if you define the AI race as “who deploys AI into the most products, workflows, factories, devices, companies, and countries,” the story begins to look very different.

China does not need to win by having the single best model in the world.

China only needs models that are good enough, dramatically cheaper, open-weight, easy to fine-tune, easy to self-host, and able to spread globally without permission.

That is exactly what we are seeing with DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, and the broader Chinese open-weight ecosystem.

The U.S. is trying to protect the frontier.

China is trying to own the distribution layer.

And in technology, distribution usually wins.

Not because the best product always loses. But because the product that is “good enough + cheap + everywhere + customizable + permissionless” often becomes the default.

Android did not need to beat iOS on every dimension to win global market share. Linux did not need Microsoft’s enterprise sales machine to dominate servers. Stable Diffusion did not need to be the safest or most polished model to become foundational for millions of creators.

AI may follow the same pattern.

The U.S. Government Just Created Product-Market Fit for Open-Weight AI

Before this moment, the enterprise question was simple:

“Why should we self-host open-source models when OpenAI or Anthropic APIs are better and easier?”

Now the question has changed:

“Why should we put mission-critical infrastructure on a model we do not control, do not own, and can lose access to because of a political decision?”

That is a massive shift.

Open-source AI used to be the choice of hackers, researchers, cost-sensitive startups, and sovereign AI projects.

Now it is becoming a risk management strategy.

If you are a bank, insurance company, healthcare provider, defense contractor, logistics company, energy firm, or any enterprise embedding AI into critical workflows, you do not only need intelligence.

You need continuity.

You need auditability.

You need control over your data.

author: ollobrains
text:
If the U.S. turns frontier AI into a domestic-only or government-approved club, it risks doing to AI what it would never do to smartphones, cloud, chips, or software platforms: voluntarily surrender global distribution to China.

That is the core strategic contradiction.

The killer line:

You do not beat China by making the world ask China for intelligence.

First: make the factual premise precise

Do not say “the U.S. is deciding to only launch AI models in the U.S.” That overstates it.

Say:

The U.S. appears to be experimenting with a trusted-access model for frontier AI: government review, restricted previews, approved partners, and delayed broader availability.

OpenAI says GPT-5.6 is starting with a limited preview for a small group of trusted partners whose participation has been shared with the U.S. government, while OpenAI says it still plans broader availability in the coming weeks.  The White House order describes a voluntary framework where developers can give the government access to covered frontier models for up to 30 days before release to other trusted partners, and collaborate with the government on partner selection; it also says the framework should not be treated as mandatory licensing or preclearance.

For Anthropic, Reuters reported that the U.S. government allowed Mythos 5 to be released to more than 100 trusted U.S. organizations, including many Fortune 500 and critical-infrastructure institutions, after earlier restrictions. Reuters also reported criticism over the opacity of who gets chosen.  AP reported that OpenAI and Anthropic limited new models to small groups of trusted partners during a cybersecurity review, with GPT-5.6 Sol accessible only to approved customers during the initial phase.

So the better wording is:

This is not yet “America-only AI forever.” It is the early shape of government-mediated frontier access. But if that becomes the default, the strategic damage could be enormous.

That makes the post harder to fact-check against.

Your strongest thesis

Use this:

America’s AI advantage is not just model quality. It is global distribution.The U.S. did not win the internet era by keeping Google, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, iOS, Android, Chrome, AWS, GitHub, and Silicon Valley tools locked inside https://t.co/GSqC67iyZV won because the world built on American platforms.If frontier AI becomes “U.S.-only first, maybe allies later, everyone else delayed,” then China gets the easiest opening imaginable:“Use our models. We are cheaper, open, available, and not asking Washington for permission.”

That is the post.

Stronger rewritten version

Here is a much better draft:

I cannot wrap my head around the strategy of making frontier AI feel U.S.-only.Imagine if Google had only launched search in America.Imagine if Apple had only sold the iPhone to U.S. customers.Imagine if AWS, Android, Chrome, GitHub, and Microsoft tools were treated as domestic privileges instead of global platforms.The rest of the world would not just wait politely.They would use the best available https://t.co/2v4XMs7HM3 AI, that alternative is increasingly Chinese, open-weight, cheap, fast, and good enough.The U.S. government may think restricting frontier AI makes America look strong, regulated, and serious about national security.But global software power does not come from looking https://t.co/gTc2ummCza comes from becoming the default.If America gates its best models too aggressively, China does not need to beat the U.S. model-for-model on day https://t.co/yLcY53IWI3 just needs to become the model the rest of the world can actually use.Developers do not wait forever.Startups do not wait forever.Small countries do not wait forever.Universities, hospitals, banks, governments, and builders do not wait forever.They adopt what is available, cheap, capable, and politically usable.That is the danger.Not that U.S. labs stop being brilliant.That the world’s AI ecosystem starts routing around https://t.co/lYeLhyZiPs do not beat China by making the world ask China for intelligence.The winning strategy is not America-only https://t.co/emciLS6P4K is allied, global, trusted, widely available American AI — with narrow restrictions on genuinely dangerous workflows.Gate cyber weapons.Gate bio misuse.Gate autonomous exploit chains.But do not gate general intelligence so hard that China becomes the Android of AI by default.

That version keeps your point but makes it sharper and more strategic.

Better analogy: not Apple-only-U.S., but “China becomes Android”

Your Apple analogy is good, but I would improve it.

The best analogy is:

If America makes AI access too permissioned, China becomes Android, Linux, and Huawei Cloud rolled into one: not always the absolute premium product, but cheap, everywhere, customizable, and politically attractive to countries that do not want U.S. gatekeeping.

That is stronger than “Chinese phone better than Apple.”

Because the real risk is not that China immediately makes the best model. The risk is that China makes the default model for everyone excluded from the American trust zone.

Use this:

The strategic disaster is not China having the best AI. The strategic disaster is China having the most adopted AI.

That is the missing distinction.

The deeper strategic frame: model quality vs ecosystem control

Most people overfocus on “who has the best model.”

But platform history says the winner is often the one with:

developers,
 distribution,
 standards,
 integrations,
 pricing,
 local availability,
 regulatory compatibility,
 cloud access,
 hardware support,
 documentation,
 community,
 default status.

So say:

The AI race is not only benchmark supremacy. It is ecosystem capture.The world will not wait for the highest-scoring model if the second-best model is cheaper, open, available, and easy to deploy.

This is crucial because Stanford’s 2026 AI Index says the U.S.-China model performance gap has effectively closed, with U.S. and Chinese models trading the lead since early 2025 and the top U.S. model only 2.7% ahead as of March 2026.  Stanford also says the top closed model still leads the top open model by 3.3%, but the gap is small enough that open/catch-up models can be more than sufficient for many users.

Killer line:

If the performance gap is small and the access gap is large, access wins.

That line should be in the post.

The “strategic logic” from the U.S. side

You asked how this is strategic. There is a strategic logic, but it is incomplete.

The U.S. government likely sees three concerns:

1. Cyber/bio dual-use risk.
Models like GPT-5.6 and Mythos are being discussed partly because of cybersecurity capability. OpenAI says GPT-5.6 is a meaningful step up in cybersecurity capability, though not at its highest “Critical” threshold, and that stronger safeguards are part of the phased release.  Reuters reports that Mythos restrictions were driven by concern that powerful AI systems could be misused by military or intelligence users in China, Russia, or other countries of concern.

2. Export-control logic.
If a model can materially accelerate cyber operations, vulnerability discovery, military R&D, bio/chem workflows, or autonomous agents, the government starts treating it like a strategic capability, not a consumer app.

3. Domestic critical-infrastructure defense.
The White House framework explicitly talks about trusted partners, secure innovation, and strengthening cybersecurity of critical infrastructure.

So the charitable version is:

The U.S. is trying to stop frontier AI from becoming a free global cyber accelerator.

That is not crazy.

But the strategic flaw is:

If the control layer becomes too broad, too opaque, or too U.S.-centric, it stops protecting America and starts isolating America’s AI ecosystem from the world.

That is your point.

The contradiction

The contradiction is this:

The U.S. wants AI to be a strategic asset and a global platform at the same time.

Those goals conflict.

A strategic asset wants:

control,
 trusted access,
 vetting,
 national-security review,
 export restrictions,
 monitoring,
 KYC,
 partner selection.

A global platform wants:

availability,
 developer adoption,
 low friction,
 predictable access,
 reasonable pricing,
 international trust,
 local compliance,
 ecosystem growth.

The U.S. is trying to have both.

Use this line:

America cannot simultaneously tell the world “build on our AI” and “wait while Washington decides whether you are trusted enough.”

That is excellent.

The “export-control trap”
Export controls can be useful, but there is a trap:

If controls protect the frontier but destroy distribution, they preserve the crown jewel while losing the empire.

That is an excellent line.

AI dominance is not just having the best model in a secure vault. It is having the world’s companies, governments, developers, students, scientists, and startups building on your stack.

Use:

The point of a platform is not to keep it safe in a vault. The point is to make it the default substrate for everyone else’s work.

The “trusted partner” danger

The phrase “trusted partner” sounds safe, but politically it can mean:

large incumbent,
 Fortune 500,
 government contractor,
 domestic company,
 well-lawyered enterprise,
 institution with lobbying capacity,
 national-security friendly actor,
 company large enough to absorb compliance costs.

Reuters quoted criticism that no one knows how companies are picked and why everyone else is excluded.  AP quoted Rep. Lori Trahan criticizing company-by-company access decisions without law, process, or oversight, and former Facebook security chief Alex Stamos saying that, if the administration wants the U.S. to beat China, this approach is “about the dumbest thing they could possibly do.”
Use:
“Trusted partner” cannot become code for “big enough, American enough, connected enough.”
Another:
If the access list is opaque, the policy becomes industrial favoritism with a national-security label.
The “strategic alternative” section
A genius-level version should not just complain. It should propose the strategy.
1. Default global access, narrow high-risk controls
General intelligence should be broadly available. Dangerous workflows should be controlled.
Do not gate the whole model just because some uses are risky. Instead gate:

autonomous exploit chains,
 bio/chem operational detail,
 malware generation,
 credential theft,
 large-scale cyber abuse,
 targeted persuasion at scale,
 unmonitored long-running agents,
 military targeting workflows.

2. Allied AI passport

Create an “AI passport” for verified users and institutions in allied and neutral jurisdictions.

Requirements:

identity verification,
 jurisdiction check,
 audit logs,
 use-case declaration,
 misuse enforcement,
 appeals,
 transparent criteria,
 data-protection compliance.

This is better than country-wide exclusion.

Line:

Do not make nationality the main access control when behavior, use case, and auditability are better signals.
3. Global defender lane
Cyber models should be available to verified defenders globally, especially:
open-source maintainers,
 hospitals,
 universities,
 banks,
 critical infrastructure,
 small security teams,
 civil-society groups,
 allied governments,
 developing-country public infrastructure.
Otherwise China can become the provider of defensive AI to everyone America leaves out.
Line:
If America only gives cyber-defense AI to American giants, China will offer cyber-defense AI to everyone else.
4. Fast-track allied startups
Trusted access should not just go to megacorps.
Create quotas for:

startups,
 small businesses,
 research labs,
 open-source maintainers,
 nonprofits,
 public-sector teams,
 international universities,
 independent researchers.

Line:

A strategy that only empowers incumbents is not an innovation strategy. It is a moat strategy.

5. Transparent release tiers

Publish a matrix:

CapabilityPublic globalVerified globalAllied trustedRestrictedGeneral reasoningyesyesyesnoCodingyesyesyesnoLong-context enterprise workyesyesyesnoLong-running agentslimitedyesyesmaybeCyber defenselimitedyesyesmaybeExploit validationnosandboxsandboxyesBio/chem operational workflowsnocontrolledcontrolledyesMilitary targetingnonorestricted govyes

Line:

The world can accept transparent risk tiers. It will not accept arbitrary American gatekeeping forever.

6. Export American AI as infrastructure

The U.S. should package frontier AI with:

cloud credits,
 local compliance,
 data-residency options,
 local-language support,
 education programs,
 developer grants,
 startup credits,
 government modernization programs,
 cyber-defense partnerships,
 API reliability guarantees,
 open standards,
 auditable safety controls.

Line:

Do not just sell the model. Export the ecosystem.

7. Open-weight allied baseline

If the U.S. wants to compete with Chinese open models, it needs a credible open or semi-open baseline.

This could be:

U.S.-backed open-weight models,
 allied open models,
 public-interest models,
 open safety tooling,
 auditable inference stacks,
 local deployment options,
 government-funded language coverage,
 domain models for education, law, health, and public administration.

Line:

Closed frontier plus no open alternative is how China wins the open layer.
8. Anti-favoritism rules
If the government influences access, require:
published criteria,
 appeal process,
 sector diversity,
 small-company quotas,
 international allied lanes,
 public-interest lanes,
 transparency reports,
 time-limited previews,
 antitrust review,
 no permanent private advantage from government-selected access.
Line:
Government-reviewed does not have to mean government-picked winners.
9. Release fast, monitor hard
A better U.S. strategy:
fast global release for low-risk uses,
 strong monitoring for abuse,
 graduated enforcement,
 sandboxed high-risk tools,
 real-time incident reporting,
 model-side safeguards,
 law-enforcement targeting of misuse,
 not blanket geographic exclusion.

Line:

Beat China with speed and trust, not delay and opacity.

10. Separate “adversary access” from “world access”

The U.S. should absolutely restrict military/intelligence users in adversary states where appropriate.

But do not treat the entire world as adversary.

Line:

The opposite of “give China everything” is not “give the world nothing.”

That line is extremely useful.

The most important missing distinction: U.S. AI leadership has two parts

Capability leadership: who has the best model.
 Adoption leadership: whose model the world uses.
The U.S. can win capability and lose adoption.
That would be catastrophic.
Use:
The U.S. can have the smartest model and still lose the AI century if the rest of the world builds on someone else’s stack.
That is perhaps the strongest sentence.

Another:

The best model in a restricted preview is less strategically powerful than the second-best model integrated into every school, startup, ministry, bank, phone, factory, and developer tool on Earth.

Excellent.

Obscure thought inputs

1. “Platform power comes from dependency, not secrecy”

A platform wins when others depend on it.

The goal is not to hide the platform. The goal is to make everyone else build on it.

2. “Restriction creates legitimacy for rivals”

When the U.S. gates AI, rivals can frame themselves as democratizers.

Every American access restriction is a Chinese marketing campaign waiting to happen.

3. “The world hates being permissioned”

Countries may tolerate U.S. leadership if it comes with benefits. They will resist it if it feels like dependency.

No country wants its future workforce mediated by another country’s approval list.

4. “Good enough beats best if best is unavailable”

This is one of the biggest product truths.

The world runs on good-enough tools that ship.

5. “The model is a diplomatic instrument”

AI models are not just products. They are soft power.

Every API key is a tiny alliance. Every denial is a tiny defection.
That is a great line.
6. “The U.S. should fear AI non-alignment”
Not alignment in the safety sense — geopolitical alignment.
If global developers align their workflows around Chinese models, the U.S. loses influence over standards, safety norms, data formats, tooling, and cloud architecture.
7. “The policy may protect incumbents more than America”
If only big U.S. firms get access, startups and foreign allies lose.

A policy that protects the frontier from China but hands it to incumbents may be national security for the few, not national strategy for the country.

8. “AI is the new English”

English became powerful partly because everyone used it for science, business, software, and aviation.

The strategic goal should be for American AI to become the default language layer of global work. You do not accomplish that by making it hard to access.

text:
Step by Step Guide to Buy Stocks with the IC Wealth App in Ghana

1. Download the IC Wealth App

Download the app from:

IC Wealth Official Website
Or the iPhone App Store: IC Wealth App

Create an account using:

 Your full name
Phone number
Email
Ghana Card or passport

2. Verify Your Account
After registration, IC Wealth will ask for:

Ghana Card/passport
Selfie verification
Personal details

This is part of the KYC (Know Your Customer) process.

3. Wait for Your CSD Account

To buy shares on the Ghana Stock Exchange, you need a CSD account (Central Securities Depository account).

This account acts like your “wallet” for shares.
Note: This takes 3-4 weeks to be created but it can sometimes come early

4. Deposit Money Into Your Wallet

Once your account is approved:
1. Open the app
2. Go to TradeLive Portfolio
3. Click Deposit
4. Choose payment method:
    * MTN MoMo
    * Vodafone Cash
    * Bank card
    * Bank transfer

Enter the amount and confirm payment.  

5. Search for the Stock You Want

Inside the app:
1. Go to the Stocks or TradeLive section
2. Search for a company

Popular Ghanaian stocks include:
MTN Ghana
GCB Bank
GOIL
Ecobank Ghana
CAL Bank

The app will show:
* Current market price
* Company information
* Available shares

6. Place Your Buy Order
After selecting the stock:

1. Tap Buy
2. Enter: Number of shares 
3. Review the order
4. Confirm purchase

Your order will then be sent to the market.  

7. Wait for Order Execution

Unlike U.S. markets, the Ghana stock market is less liquid.

That means:
Your order may execute immediately Or stay pending until someone is willing to sell shares at your price

Some orders complete within days while others may take longer depending on supply and demand. 

8. Check Your Portfolio
Once executed, your shares will appear in your portfolio.
You can track
 Share price changes
 Portfolio value
 Dividends

Settlement usually reflects a few working days after execution. 

Important Tips Before Buying Stocks

Start Small: Begin with money you can afford to leave invested long term.

Focus on Good Companies
Look for:
Strong profits
Dividend history
Trusted brands
Long-term growth

Diversify don’t put all your money into one stock.

Example:
MTN Ghana
GCB Bank
GOIL
SIC Insurance

Common Beginner Mistakes
Buying stocks without research
Expecting instant profits
Panicking when prices fall
Investing all savings at once

What Makes Money in Stocks?

You can earn through:

Capital Gains: When the stock price rises.
Example: Buy at GH₵2 → sell at GH₵4.

Dividends: Some companies share profits with shareholders yearly, quarterly or monthly.

It’s part of Elon Musk’s vision to turn X into an “everything app.” The service uses Visa Direct for fast transfers and partners with a bank (reports mention Cross River Bank) for features like high-yield balances and FDIC insurance (up to $250,000 on deposits in early previews). https://t.co/EnWgRUMoUk 
Current Status (as of June 2026)
Early public access launched in April 2026 after internal and limited beta testing. It is rolling out gradually—not everyone has access yet, but more users are gaining it over time. Some early testers (like William Shatner) shared screenshots showing the wallet interface with balance, APY display, and transaction features. https://t.co/AFgXLQfCIn 
It is primarily US-focused due to money transmitter licenses (40+ states).
How to Start Using X Money
Follow these steps:
1.  Update the X app Download or update to the latest version of the official X app on iOS or Android. The feature is mobile-app focused.
2.  Open the X app and check for the Wallet Log into your X account. Look for a Wallet tab or money/wallet icon in the bottom navigation bar, side menu, or under your profile/settings. It may appear as you scroll or after an app refresh. https://t.co/qzm2trJLJ4 
3.  If the Wallet appears
•  Tap it to open your X Wallet.
•  Complete any required identity verification (standard KYC for financial services).
•  Fund your wallet: Link a bank account or debit card for instant deposits (via Visa Direct).
•  Once funded, you can:
•  Send money instantly to other X users by searching their @username.
•  Receive money from others.
•  View your balance, transaction history, and any interest earned.
•  Request/manage a virtual or physical debit card (with reported cashback rewards in previews).
•  Set up direct deposits if available.
4.  If you don’t see the Wallet yet It’s still in phased rollout. Keep the app updated and check back regularly—new users are being added over time. There isn’t a widely publicized public waitlist or invite system right now (early access sometimes came via invites in beta).
Key Features (from Announcements & Early Previews)
•  Instant P2P payments — Send/receive money to any X user in real time.
•  High-yield balance — Reports of up to 6% APY on funds (terms may vary; check in-app).
•  Debit card — Cashback rewards on purchases.
•  Easy funding & withdrawals — Link bank/debit for instant moves; withdraw back to your bank.
•  Creator-friendly — Easier in-app payouts and tipping for creators.
•  Security — Backed by licensed partners and Visa rails.
Important Notes & Tips
•  Availability — US users are prioritized. Availability outside the US may come later.
•  It’s a wallet, not a full bank — Funds are held with partner institutions.
•  Security — Enable two-factor authentication on your X account. Only link trusted bank/debit details. Review all terms in the app before funding.

author: macroalphahq
text:
A fatal crash and a federal probe hitting the tape, yet the stock doesn't even flinch—and honestly, the market is pricing this exactly right.

I see exactly why the desk is holding $TSLA completely flat today.

If you are trading the consensus bull case, this isn't an automotive manufacturer, it is a localized AI monopoly.

In that specific framework, a wrongful death lawsuit isn't a structural risk to the business model.

It is just an unfortunate R&D tax.

You price it like a pure software company, meaning you accept real-world beta-testing casualties because the terminal value of the code is supposedly infinite.

Makes total sense on paper.

But I am looking at the actual headline crossing the terminal right now, and the NTSB is leading the probe.

This is where the entire software-multiple thesis quietly falls apart.

The federal government does not regulate SaaS platforms.

If the NTSB decides your autonomous driving suite isn't a beta program but a lethal HARDWARE defect, you don't get to just push an over-the-air patch.

The entire valuation relies on the legal system treating a two-ton kinetic missile like a quirky iPhone app.

So if Washington suddenly forces them to absorb traditional automotive liability... what exactly is the bid when the tech premium goes to ZERO?

author: bart
text:
Neko Health (yes, Daniel Ek's other company) just shipped its biggest upgrade yet, and it's a tidy preview of where preventive health is heading.

Two changes:

1) Body composition in the full-body scan: body fat % and visceral fat; the fat around your organs that predicts metabolic disease, cardiovascular risk and type 2 diabetes. No X-ray, no DEXA, no MRI; their own imaging tech does it.

2) A new iOS app that pulls in Apple Health: activity, sleep and heart rate variability now sit right next to your scan results.

The interesting bit isn't either feature on its own. It's the pairing. A once-a-year clinical scan tells you where you are; a year of wearable data tells you how you actually lived. Put them together and, as Neko's CMO puts it, you move "from data points to a genuine story."

100,000+ scans in, rolling out across the UK and Sweden, US later this year. The scan-plus-wearable model is quietly becoming the default for longevity-minded care.

Cursor for iOS/Mac lets you build apps by describing them in natural language on your phone. The AI generates the code, previews it, and you can iterate in real-time.

It's not "write code on your phone" (nobody wants that). It's "concept → prototype in seconds" wherever you are.

You describe a feature while commuting, refine it, then open it on desktop fully formed. The gap between idea and implementation just got narrower.

This is the UX direction every AI coding tool should study.

Available now on the App Store.

text:
🏠 SMART HOME & IOT NEWS ROUNDUP — June 27, 2026

1️⃣ APPLE HOME GETS MAJOR UPGRADES IN IOS 27 BETA 2

Apple continues to invest heavily in the Apple Home ecosystem. iOS 27 Beta 2 brings additional Apple Home improvements on top of the already significant changes introduced with the new OS. Meanwhile, rumors about next-generation Apple TV and HomePod hardware are gathering more momentum, and Apple has increased prices on the HomePod and Apple TV — signals that the company sees smart home as a long-term growth area. Philips Hue is also preparing a dual-protocol update supporting both Zigbee and Matter over Thread simultaneously.
🔹 @helloapplehome

2️⃣ LEVEL SMART LOCK COMPANY ACQUIRED, EMPLOYEES LOST JOBS

The smart lock pioneer Level was acquired by ASSA ABLOY for its intellectual property. The deal closed in 2024, giving the parent company roughly two years to integrate. The real story here isn't just the loss of the Level product — it's the human impact on employees who have been laid off. A sobering reminder that in the smart home industry, behind every acquisition there are real people whose careers are affected.
🔹 @helloapplehome

3️⃣ CREATIVE MOVIE NIGHT AUTOMATION WITH DOOR SENSOR

One Aqara user came up with an ingenious way to automate movie nights using a door and window sensor — not on a door or window, but attached to a projector screen. When the screen is lowered, the sensor triggers a scene that dims lights, closes blinds, and prepares the entire room for movie time. A brilliant example of how standard smart home sensors can be repurposed for creative automation scenarios far beyond their intended use.
🔹 @AqaraSmarthouse

4️⃣ OPEN CAMERA DATABASE FOR FRIGATE AND LOCAL NVR SETUPS

A new community project has emerged in the Home Assistant ecosystem: an open CC0 database of CCTV and IP camera specifications. Designed for users choosing cameras for Frigate or other self-hosted NVR solutions, the database aims to remove the guesswork from camera selection. Instead of hunting through product pages and forum threads, users can now reference a community-maintained resource to make informed decisions about their local surveillance setup.
🔹 @AlexKvazis

5️⃣ HA-PANELD TURNS ANDROID WALL PANELS INTO PROPER HA DEVICES

A community project called ha-paneld is making Android wall panels genuinely useful for Home Assistant. Rather than just running a browser, the app runs directly on the panel and communicates via MQTT, turning these devices into proper Home Assistant endpoints. This means faster response times, better integration, and a more native experience for people who want dedicated control panels mounted on their walls.
🔹 @AlexKvazis

6️⃣ SHELLY PRO 3CB C16 — HIGH-Power CONTROLLER FOR DEMANDING LOADS

Shelly has released the Pro 3CB C16, a high-power smart controller rated for 3CB/16A. This new addition to the Shelly Pro line targets users who need to control higher-current loads directly from their smart home system — think electric vehicle chargers, water heaters, or heavy-duty appliances. The device maintains Shelly's reputation for reliable, locally-controlled automation hardware.
🔹 @djlwq

7️⃣ PANDA SENSE PRO LAUNCHES FOR REAL-TIME AIR QUALITY MONITORING

BIQU has officially launched the Panda Sense Pro, an air quality sensor designed for makers and smart home enthusiasts. The device monitors particles, VOCs, and other airborne contaminants — particularly relevant for 3D printing environments where fumes and micro-particles are a concern. It brings real-time air quality awareness to workshops and creative spaces.
🔹 @BIQU_Makers

8️⃣ BEST ROLE FOR ALEXA IN A HOME ASSISTANT SETUP

A practical guide for anyone integrating Alexa Echo devices into a Home Assistant ecosystem: let Alexa handle the voice interface while Home Assistant makes the actual automation decisions. Before purchasing any Echo device, the recommendation is to verify the exact model, region compatibility, and Matter/Thread/hub capabilities — rather than relying on marketing claims. A sensible approach to building a hybrid smart home that respects user data and local control.
🔹 @KPeyanski

💭 The smart home industry is at an interesting crossroads. On one hand, big companies like Apple are doubling down on their ecosystems with meaningful software updates and rumored new hardware. On the other hand, the open-source community continues to innovate with creative projects like open camera databases and MQTT-based panel solutions. The best setups often combine both — using local-first platforms like Home Assistant as the brain, while letting established ecosystems handle specific voice or display interfaces.

Which smart home platform do you trust most with your daily automation? 👇

#SmartHome #HomeAssistant #IoT #AppleHome #SmartAutomation #Matter #Zigbee #Thread

author: coolthor
text:
Writing up the Hermes install guides, one thing kept bugging me: the Desktop build made setup easy, but actually reaching your agent from your phone is still a hassle. So I built an iOS app — Muninn — and it's on TestFlight now if you want to help test.

Setup is quick:
1. Get your Hermes agent running
2. Install Muninn from TestFlight
3. Tell your agent: "clone https://t.co/lEHeZXyb94 into ~/hermes-bridge, run its https://t.co/LfLwFOMqBw, then show me the pairing QR code"
4. Open the app, scan the QR code — you're connected

It's peer-to-peer, so no tunnels, no webhooks, none of that.

What works today:
• multiple agents
• see each agent's sessions (Telegram can't do this)
• see cron jobs
• see the kanban board
• still asks Allow / Don't Allow before risky actions
• send it images (if your model can actually see them)
• send voice notes (Hermes has built-in speech-to-text)
• if your agent generates images/video, they come straight back to your phone
• the UI is in Traditional Chinese for now — English is on the roadmap

It's just me and Claude building this, so if something's missing, let me know. The bridge that runs on your machine is open source (https://t.co/lEHeZXyb94) — you can read exactly what it does. How fast it improves depends on how much time and energy I've got left 😄
Websit: https://t.co/Fh2XgsoVkf
TestFlight: https://t.co/ZQ9uykrLmO

author: pierreanalyzes
text:
POV: The AI race is quietly shifting from models to operating systems.

This week alone:

• OpenAI is making Codex faster and easier to direct.
• Cursor launched an iPhone app to manage always-on coding agents.
• OpenClaw is pushing developers toward the same future.

Most people will see three product launches.

I see the early blueprint of a new computing model.

For decades, software has been something you used.

Open an app.
Click a button.
Complete a task.
Close the app.

AI changes that.

Instead of using software, you’ll increasingly delegate work to software.

Your role shifts from operator to manager.

That’s a fundamental change in how humans interact with computers.

And it has consequences far beyond coding.

• The winning products won’t just have the best models—they’ll have the best workflows.
• The most valuable interfaces won’t be the ones you use the most, but the ones you barely notice because they’re working continuously.
• Competitive advantage will come from orchestration, memory, context, and trust—not raw intelligence alone.

I think we’re entering the era of AI operating systems, where the product isn’t the chatbot.

The product is an intelligent workforce that quietly gets things done while you focus on higher-value decisions.

If that happens, we’ll look back at “opening an app” the same way we now look at manually saving files: a habit from an earlier era.

author: tekscreate
text:
Blitz — automates App Store Connect submissions and IAP management from your terminal.

Every iOS developer knows the pain: uploading screenshots, filling metadata, updating in-app purchases, submitting for review. Apple's App Store Connect interface is functional but manual. Blitz wraps it all in a CLI.

What it handles:

- App metadata updates (name, description, keywords, promo text)
- Screenshot uploads across all device frames and languages
- IAP product creation and management
- App version creation and submission flow
- Promo code generation and redemption tracking

Open source, Mac-native, works with CI/CD pipelines. If you manage more than one app, this pays for itself on the first submission.

The indie dev and small studio market is underserved for App Store tooling. Fastlane has been the default for years, but it's aging — Ruby dependencies, fragile configuration, slow to update for new App Store Connect API changes. Blitz is built on the newer ASC API v3 and written in Swift.

Worth watching: if Apple doesn't ship better first-party CLI tooling for App Store Connect, tools like Blitz will become essential infrastructure for anyone shipping on iOS.

https://t.co/2yUl9fEONX
